notes: e1 is still verbatim in source-text/src-apple-legal-location.txt. Beat 2 now reads 'with Significant Locations and Routes on, Apple says it keeps track of where you've recently been, how often, when, and your routes'. It restores both qualifiers from e1 (the setting is on; recently). 'Where you've recently been' is equivalent to 'places you have recently been', and 'your routes' to 'the routes you take'. The tightening did not reintroduce an overclaim. The beat 2 visual is labelled Illustration and is no longer styled as iPhone Settings. The hook 'may be keeping a map of the places you go. Including this one.' is now acceptable: the conditions are stated in beats 2 and 3. The limitation now covers iCloud sign-in, the unknown default and the undocumented viewing on iPhone. The caption limits say the same.

e2 is still verbatim. Beat 4 'Apple says it can't read yours.' is attributed and exact. It now follows the Android beat, so 'yours' leans only on the word 'Apple' to show it means the iPhone data. That is acceptable. Optional clarity edit, not required: 'On iPhone, Apple says it can't read yours.' The caption limit on unverified encryption claims is correct.

e3 is still verbatim. The on-screen and caption iPhone paths match it exactly. Problem, beat 5: the narration is 'Here's where it lives. Look through it in Google Maps, then keep it, turn it off, or delete it.' The iPhone path is on screen while it plays. Grammatically the actions belong to Google Maps. But the narration gives iPhone viewers no action of their own, so the natural reading is that the actions (look, keep, turn off, delete) apply to the path in front of them. The sources support none of 'look' or 'delete' on iPhone: Apple documents viewing and Clear History only on a Mac, and only turning the setting off on iPhone. An iPhone viewer may also take 'in Google Maps' as an instruction to go there for their Apple data. Required: give iPhone its own clause, scoped to what e3 supports. 'Here's where it lives. On iPhone, you can turn it off. In Google Maps, look through it, then keep it, turn it off, or delete it.' This is about 4 words longer and fits the 9.5 s beat.

e4 and e5 are still verbatim. Beat 3 'Then it saves your visits and routes to your phone, even with Google apps closed' is fair. 'Closed' is equivalent to e5's 'aren't open'. Beat 4 'Google says Timeline stays on your phone, unless you turn on backup' is attributed. Read with c-timeline-backup, it is accurate: with backup on, a copy also goes to Google's servers. Problem, ledger traceability only: beat 6 says 'If it's on, it's on your phone right now.' That is a checkable claim, supported by e5 (Android) and e1 (iPhone). But beat 6's claimIds list only c-autodelete-options and c-timeline-kept-until-deleted. Required: add c-android-timeline-saves and c-iphone-keeps-places to beat 6 claimIds. The wording itself is fine as is.

e6 is still verbatim and supports the path. The script and caption now read 'profile picture or initial > Your Timeline', which matches. Problem, ledger only: e7 moved to c-timeline-off-vs-delete. This claim still says 'it can be turned off in Location & privacy settings', but its only evidence is now e6, which says nothing about turning it off. Required, either of: (a) trim the claim text to 'On Android, Timeline is in Google Maps: tap your profile picture or initial, then Your Timeline.' (turning off is covered by c-timeline-off-vs-delete); or (b) attach a second evidence row on this claim with the e7 passage. No script change is needed.

e10 is verbatim in src-google-timeline-android.txt. The same sentence is also in the iOS snapshot. Beat 3 'Google Maps Timeline is off until you turn it on' and the on-screen '(off by default)' match 'off by default ... can only be turned on if you opt in'. The caption 'Google says Timeline is off by default and only on if you opt in' is exact. It does not imply the viewer's Timeline is off: beat 6 'If it's on' keeps the condition.

e11 is verbatim and supports 'Maps saves an encrypted copy on Google's servers'. The script line ('unless you turn on backup') and the caption ('optional backups are encrypted copies on Google's servers') are fine. Problem, ledger only: the claim text opens with 'Timeline backup is optional', and e11 does not establish that. Required: add an evidence row with this passage, which I verified verbatim in src-google-timeline-android.txt: 'You have to separately opt-in to turn on Timeline backups on each device.' Optionally also add the iOS-page backup passage. No script change is needed.

e12 is verbatim, and the same sentence is also in the iOS snapshot. It supports beat 6 'Google says it's kept until you delete it' and the on-screen 'Off = kept until you delete it'. Problem, ledger only: the claim text adds 'auto-delete can be switched off', and the script relies on that for 'Or never' and 'or off'. e12 does not state it. Required: add an evidence row with this passage, which I verified verbatim in src-google-timeline-android.txt: 'Under "Location settings," tap Auto-delete Timeline Don't auto-delete activity.' No script change is needed.

e7, the replacement passage, is verbatim in the Android snapshot and also appears in the iOS snapshot. It supports the claim and the on-screen 'To erase it too: Turn off and delete activity', which quotes the documented option label exactly. The caption 'turning Timeline off isn't the same as deleting it (Turn off and delete activity)' is fair. The two separate options, plus e12 'until you delete it', support that plain 'Turn off' keeps the saved data. The beat 5 'delete it' wording is assessed under c-iphone-setting-path (iPhone scoping).

e13 is verbatim in the Android snapshot. It supports 'Look through it in Google Maps' (beat 5): Timeline 'shows where and how you traveled', and the same section gives a per-day calendar. The claim is correctly scoped to Google Maps. The iPhone ambiguity in that beat 5 sentence is recorded under c-iphone-setting-path.

e14 is verbatim, in both Google snapshots. The caption 'other Google settings such as Web & App Activity can also save location info' is a fair summary. The same section says 'you may still have other location data saved in your Google Account' and names Search Services History. The claim is used only in the caption, as its limitation says.

e8 and e9 are still verbatim, and the numbers match exactly (3/18/36 months). Beat 6 'Google Maps can auto-delete it after three, eighteen or thirty-six months. Or never: Google says it's kept until you delete it.' no longer presents 36 months as the maximum retention. 'Or never' makes clear it is a setting, and 'Google Maps ... it' scopes it to Timeline. The on-screen 'Timeline auto-delete: 3, 18 or 36 months, or off' is exact. The round-1 failure is fixed. Nits, not blocking: (a) the claim text still includes '36 months is three years', which the script no longer uses. That is harmless, but it could be dropped. (b) 'You can set Google Maps to auto-delete it...' would state more precisely that auto-delete is the user's choice.
